input.quote: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
input.rationale: Section 9 is mutual in form and mutually excludes indirect/consequential damages, and it places Section 8 (Commerce One's IP infringement indemnity) outside both the cap and the consequential-damages exclusion. However it fails the fallback on two material terms. First, the cap is not twelve months' fees: it is only the amount "ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO ... FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO" in the prior twelve months, which slices the cap down to a single transaction's fees (under Exhibit B pricing, potentially a small per-transaction or revenue-share amount) and can fall well below six months' fees — walk-away territory for a vendor cap. Second, the only carve-out is Section 8; the fallback requires carve-outs at least for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct, and confidentiality (Section 10) plus gross negligence/willful misconduct are all inside the cap. Redline moves to the preferred position: greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, measured from the event giving rise to liability, with an "Excluded Claims" definition covering Section 8 indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud. We left the mutual consequential-damages exclusion untouched. Note p0092 appears to be an OCR duplicate of the same sentences across a page break; the conformed text should be reconciled to the edited p0090.

ops.oldText: EXCEPT FOR LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE TOTAL AMOUNT ACTUALLY PAID BY CORIO HEREUNDER FOR THE TRANSACTION WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES TO DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE FILING OF THE CAUSE OF ACTION TO WHICH THE LIABILITY RELATES.
ops.newText: EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY'S LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT OR THE USE OR PERFORMANCE OF THE SOFTWARE EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE TOTAL AMOUNT PAID OR PAYABLE BY CORIO HEREUNDER DURING THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRIOR TO THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE LIABILITY AND (B) ONE MILLION U.S. DOLLARS (US$1,000,000). "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS LIABILITY ARISING UNDER SECTION 8 OF THIS AGREEMENT, A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY OBLIGATIONS UNDER SECTION 10, AND A PARTY'S GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILLFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We aligned the mutual cap with our position — the greater of twelve months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000 — because limiting recovery to the fees for the single "transaction which the liability relates to" can leave the cap far below twelve months' fees. We also confirmed that indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud sit outside the cap.
proposal.summary: Make the mutual cap the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, and add confidentiality, gross negligence, willful misconduct and fraud to the existing Section 8 carve-out.
